title: Ottawa SAH Rule
sources: Perry JJ et al. JAMA 2013; Perry JJ et al. (2017 prospective validation) CMAJ
purpose: Rules OUT subarachnoid haemorrhage in alert (GCS 15) patients ≥ 15 years with a new, non-traumatic headache that reached maximum intensity within 1 hour. Highly sensitive (≈ 100%), low specificity — a screening rule, not a diagnostic one.

items.label: Limited neck flexion on examination (unable to touch chin to chest or within 3 cm in patients ≥ 15 y)

interpretation.label: No criteria met — SAH effectively excluded; no further investigation for SAH required on the basis of this rule
≥ 1 criterion present — cannot exclude SAH. Investigate: non-contrast CT head; if > 6 h from onset or CT non-diagnostic, LP (xanthochromia / RBC) or CT angiography per local pathway

notes: Apply ONLY to: age ≥ 15, GCS 15, new severe atraumatic headache peaking within 1 h. EXCLUDES patients with new neuro deficit, prior aneurysm / SAH / brain tumour, or ≥ 3 similar headaches over > 6 months (established recurrent headache disorder). A non-contrast CT within 6 h of onset, read by a qualified radiologist, is itself ~ 100% sensitive for SAH and may stand alone.
buildNote: Rule — any positive criterion mandates workup; the count is not a graded risk.
